This is a tentative optimization that drops the encapsulation if `decorateRequest` and `decorateReply` has not been called. In common scenarios where most of the decorations happen top-level it can guarantee an improvement of 10% of throughput.

Fixes #3341

issue_context.title: Property access is deoptimized in hooks defined closer to the root of the application
comments:
In the current case the shape difference is only (i think) the encapsulated instance of fastify in the `request`.

In a practical case this would also change properties in `request` / `response` and even the encapsulated `instance`. In my opinion if the request/responses have the same shape within an encapsulated context it's ok.

To have the same shape within all contexts i'm not sure it's doable right now without breaking the whole design.

I'll give it a try and see if my hunch is correct. There are probably some good optimizations that we can apply for this case.

(Note that this is a much better scenario than the previous issue as the shape is determined by ahead-of-time definition vs at-request-time.)

I spent some time investigating the issue. The cost of this megamorphism is roughly 10% throughput, which is significant.

I _think_ it's possible to fix this by completely rewriting the whole decorator logic. I'm not convinced the added complexity is worth it, as decorating a value will break things anyway.

Anyway I have learned my lesson and I would not ship this in v3, but rather try to get it in v4.

---

Side note, you can disable encapsulation by using fastify-plugin and obtain the same result you are after.
